evidence: Public BDB preserves plural-in-number uses and singular/intensive referential uses instead of flattening the form into one referent.
Genesis corpus controls include God-referential and other context-sensitive uses; grammatical plurality alone cannot determine theology.
boundary: keep God / gods / divine-being referents context-governed
do not infer Trinitarian or other doctrinal conclusions from grammatical number alone

evidence: Public BDB identifies the lemma as the proper name of the God of Israel.
BDB separately discusses Masoretic reading tradition and historical pronunciation/etymology proposals, supporting the candidate's identity-versus-reading separation.
boundary: 여호와 is retained as Korean Bible reading/display convention, not asserted as a settled reconstruction of the ancient pronunciation
הוה/היה derivation proposals remain provenance/etymology metadata rather than the primary lexical gloss

evidence: Public BDB distinguishes individual father from ancestor, household/clan head and extended originator/protector uses.
The preceding root discussion itself marks proposed derivation as doubtful, matching the pinned uncertainty boundary.
boundary: biological father must not be flattened with ancestor/originator uses
divine-father language is context-specific and not imported into every occurrence

evidence: Public BDB confirms son/male child and broader descendant/member-of-class relational uses.
Genesis examples and morphology support separating kinship from age/quality/class constructions.
boundary: do not treat every בן construction as direct biological sonship
young-animal and relational constructions require local syntax/context

evidence: Public BDB headline range is come-to-pass / become / be and its Genesis forms span state, becoming and event clauses.
Pinned Genesis contexts distinguish Gen 1:2 state description from Gen 1:3 jussive/event realization.
boundary: Korean rendering must be clause-sensitive rather than one fixed gloss
tense/aspect/mood and predicative construction remain part of token-level classification

evidence: Public BDB defines man/male person and derives husband from relational context.
Genesis usage confirms sexual distinction, individual/person, and husband readings depending on syntax.
boundary: husband is contextual rather than an always-on lemma gloss
speculative root derivation remains outside the user-facing head meaning

evidence: Public BDB explicitly separates woman, wife, female-of-animals and distributive/reciprocal uses.
Genesis 2 and later contexts confirm that wife status is construction/context dependent.
boundary: woman and wife senses must remain distinct
female-animal and distributive uses remain separate from human relationship senses

evidence: Public BDB confirms Qal utter/say plus inner-speech, promise/command extensions and stem-specific passive/other uses.
Genesis contexts confirm direct speech and formulaic infinitive constructions that require syntactic separation.
boundary: speech, inner speech/thought, promise and command are not one undifferentiated sense
לֵאמֹר and finite narrative forms must be classified morphologically

evidence: Public BDB confirms the broad do/make action family with extensive contextual extensions.
Pinned OpenScriptures BDB lock identifies a separate press/squeeze homograph entry, making homograph isolation a hard boundary.
boundary: do/make/produce/prepare/execute extensions remain context-governed
the separate press/squeeze homograph must never be merged into the primary עשה sense tree

evidence: Public BDB preserves Qal see/perceive, Niphal appear/be-seen and causative show/cause-to-see distinctions.
Genesis 1:9 provides an explicit appear/be-visible control that must not be rendered as active see.
boundary: stem and syntax control active see versus appear/be-seen versus causative show
idiomatic choose/provide/inspect extensions cannot replace the lexical core
